title: Story bed: ominous
description: Bass drones through the loop seam, a muted frame-drum heartbeat with a skin click, low piano octaves with the tritone, a soft bowed-vibes drone and dissonances, the motif four times slower on piano at D4/D5.
usage: The motif version: for intros, outros and gaps between lines. Under speech prefer the -underscore version. Loops seamlessly. -26 LUFS-S with a voice pocket at 1.25-2 kHz for the narration; duck it with scripts/audio/duck.py (the band-split duck, its default). All four story beds share 75 BPM, so they can be switched on a bar line (every 3.2 s).
instruments: VCSL frame drum, bass drum, cymbal swell
selfReview: Drones, a frame-drum heartbeat, low piano octaves with the D-Ab tritone, bowed-vibes dissonances and the motif four times slower on piano, now at D4/D5 (it was D3/D2, inside Zoo's F0 range). Critic round 1 (2026-11-24): it lost 9.2 LU on the phone model, so the drones and heartbeat vanished there. A soft bowed-vibes D4/A4 drone, saturated tremolo basses and a 600-900 Hz skin click on each heartbeat carry it into a phone's range; the parts a phone cannot play came down (the concert bass drum, toms, the lowest piano) and the bus takes 3 dB off below 150 Hz. Phone loss now 5.7-6.0 LU (the critic's target: 6 or less). The bar-16 drones ring through the loop seam, so nothing re-attacks at bar 0: the restart is now 1.5 LU softer than the bar before it (it was the loop's largest step, +3.3 LU in 400 ms windows). It is the most uncomfortable bed by design. The -underscore version mutes the motif and lead lines; use it under speech.
